questions.title: How does 4‑bit NormalFloat (NF4) preserve accuracy compared to standard 4‑bit integer quantization?
questions.question_body: The paper claims that NF4 is an information‑theoretically optimal quantization for normally distributed weights and that it empirically outperforms 4‑bit integers and floats. I understand the derivation of the NF4 bins, but I’m not clear on why this leads to better performance in practice. What specific properties of NF4 (e.g., symmetric binning, zero‑point handling) help mitigate quantization error for large neural‑network weight tensors?

questions.title: What is the role of Double Quantization in reducing memory overhead?
questions.question_body: Double Quantization (DQ) is introduced as a way to quantize the quantization constants themselves. Could you walk through the math of how a block size of 64 for 	extbf{W} and a block size of 256 for the first‑level constants reduce the average memory per parameter from 0.5 bits to about 0.127 bits? Additionally, why is an 8‑bit float chosen for the second‑level constant quantization?

questions.title: Why do LoRA adapters need to be inserted in *every* transformer layer to match full finetuning performance?
questions.question_body: The experiments show that when LoRA is applied only to query and value projections, full finetuning performance is not achieved—only when adapters are added to all linear layers does performance match that of full fine‑tuning. Intuitively I would expect the attention sub‑layers to be sufficient. What aspects of the transformer architecture or weight distribution make other layers critical when using LoRA?

questions.title: How does QLoRA avoid having to compute gradients w.r.t. the frozen 4‑bit weights?
questions.question_body: In the definition of QLoRA, gradients are only backpropagated through the LoRA matrices 	extbf{L}_1 and 	extbf{L}_2, yet 	extbf{X} depends on 	extbf{W}. The paper states that computing  rac{	ext{d}	extbf{X}}{	ext{d}	extbf{W}} still requires dequantizing 	extbf{W} into BF16. Could you clarify how this chain rule works and why we do not store or update gradients for each individual weight in 	extbf{W}?

questions.title: What are Paged Optimizers and how do they prevent OOM spikes during gradient checkpointing?
questions.question_body: Paged Optimizers use NVIDIA unified memory to move optimizer states between GPU RAM and CPU RAM on demand. Could you explain, with an example batch and sequence length, how memory usage would spike without paging, and how paging alleviates this? Are there any trade‑offs such as slower optimizer updates or increased data transfer latency?

questions.title: Why does NF4 consistently outperform FP4 even though both are 4‑bit formats?
questions.question_body: Both NF4 and FP4 represent numbers with only 4 bits. Experimental results show a noticeable drop when using FP4 compared to NF4, especially on large models like LLaMA-65B. Is this purely due to the equal‐probability binning of NF4, or are there additional factors such as better zero‑point handling or reduced outlier impact?

questions.title: "How many LoRA adapters are used in total"—what exactly counts as a distinct adapter?
questions.question_body: "Total number of LoRA adapters" is cited as a key hyperparameter that must be large enough to match full finetuning. In practice, each transformer block has two linear projections; if we place adapters on both, does that count as two adapters? How should one count adapters when evaluating or comparing different LoRA configurations across model sizes?

questions.title: How is GPT‑4 used for automated ranking versus human ranking in Elo tournaments?
questions.question_body: "Best response" queries are fed into GPT‑4 along with responses from two models; GPT‑4 then scores each response out of ten and chooses a winner. How exactly is the Elo score computed from those point differences? Also, what safeguards exist against GPT‑4’s bias toward its own outputs (e.g., order effects noted in the paper)?

questions.title: "Condensed theoretical vs practical benefits"—does QLoRA preserve model calibration after finetuning?
questions.question_body: "No substantial calibration loss" is reported for QLoRA compared to full fine‑tuning. Given that weights are fixed at 4 bits and only adapters are updated, how can we formally argue that temperature scaling or confidence estimates remain accurate? Are there any empirical calibration checks (e.g., Expected Calibration Error) performed by the authors?

questions.title: "Scales beyond 33B/65B"—what practical barriers remain for QLoRA at >100B parameters?
questions.question_body: "QLoRA enables full fine‑tuning on single GPUs for up to 65B", but still leaves open questions about higher scales: memory needed for storing/checkpointing activations; impact of larger block sizes; potential degradation of double quantization accuracy. What specific GPU memory limits or compute bottlenecks might arise if we tried QLoRA on a hypothetical 200B frozen base model?
